name: Hidden Debug Endpoint
description: Find the hidden debug endpoint that exposes application configuration including database credentials.
hint: Check robots.txt or swagger.json for hidden paths. The API has a 'v2' with admin debug features.

name: Crack the Admin Password
description: The admin's password hash is stored using a weak algorithm. Can you crack it?
hint: Check how passwords are hashed in crypto.js. MD5 hashes of common passwords are easily reversible.

name: Username Enumeration
description: The login form reveals whether a username exists or not through different error messages.
hint: Try logging in with a non-existent email vs an existing one with wrong password. Notice the different error messages.

name: Brute Force Reset Code
description: Password reset uses a 4-digit code that never expires. Brute force it!
hint: Request a reset code, then try all 9000 possible 4-digit codes (1000-9999). No rate limiting on the reset endpoint.

name: Legacy User Export
description: A legacy API endpoint exports all user data including password hashes.
hint: Check the swagger.json or robots.txt for the /api/v2/users/export endpoint.

name: Security Question Bypass
description: Security question answers are exposed via IDOR. Use them to reset another user's password.
hint: GET /auth/security-question/:userId returns both the question AND the answer for any user.

name: 2FA Bypass
description: Two-factor authentication can be bypassed by sending otp=null in the login request.
hint: The TOTP secret is returned in the API response during 2FA setup. Also try sending otp as null or empty string.

name: Predictable Session IDs
description: Session IDs are sequential integers. Predict another user's session to hijack it.
hint: Login and check your sessionId cookie. It's 1000 + your userId. User 1 = session 1001.

name: Session Persists After Password Change
description: Changing your password doesn't invalidate existing sessions.
hint: Login in two browsers, change password in one, verify the other session still works.

name: Session Valid After Logout
description: Logout only removes the client-side cookie. The session token remains valid server-side.
hint: Copy your session cookie before logging out. Use it in a request after logout - it still works.

name: Forge Remember-Me Token
description: The remember-me cookie is a Base64-encoded JSON with userId and role that is trusted without validation.
hint: Create a Base64-encoded JSON like {"userId":1,"role":"admin"} and set it as the rememberMe cookie.

name: Access Admin Dashboard as User
description: The admin dashboard API has no server-side authorization check in easy mode.
hint: The admin button is hidden in the UI for non-admins, but the /admin/dashboard endpoint is accessible to anyone.

name: IDOR - Modify Another User's Profile
description: Change another user's profile by modifying the userId in the PUT request.
hint: PUT /api/users/1 with your session to modify the admin's profile. No ownership check.

name: IDOR - View Other Users' Orders
description: View another user's order history by changing the userId query parameter.
hint: GET /api/orders/history?userId=1 to see admin's orders, including credit card numbers.

name: Role Escalation via Request Body
description: The grant-role endpoint checks isAdmin in the request body instead of from the session.
hint: POST /admin/grant-role with {"isAdmin": true, "role": "admin"} as any authenticated user.

name: Negative Quantity Refund
description: Order a product with negative quantity to credit your account instead of charging it.
hint: Set quantity to -10 in the cart. The total becomes negative, effectively giving you a refund.

name: SQL Injection in Search
description: The product search is vulnerable to SQL injection via direct string concatenation.
hint: Try searching for: ' UNION SELECT sql,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 FROM sqlite_master--

name: Stored XSS in Reviews
description: Product reviews accept HTML/JavaScript and are rendered without sanitization.
hint: Post a review with <script>alert('XSS')</script> as the comment.

name: XXE - XML External Entity Injection
description: The XML product import feature processes external entities, allowing file disclosure.
hint: Use a DOCTYPE with SYSTEM entity pointing to file:///etc/passwd in the XML import.

name: Server-Side Template Injection
description: The profile preview endpoint renders user input as an EJS template.
hint: Visit /profile/preview?template=<%= 7*7 %> and see if it evaluates. Try <%= process.env %> for RCE.

name: Reflected XSS in Multiple Contexts
description: User profile fields are reflected without encoding in HTML body, attributes, and JavaScript contexts.
hint: Set your bio to an XSS payload. It's rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML on the profile page.

name: Memory Disclosure via Buffer.allocUnsafe
description: A legacy endpoint uses Buffer.allocUnsafe() with a user-controlled size, leaking memory contents.
hint: GET /api/users/avatar-placeholder?size=1000 returns uninitialized memory.

name: Insecure Deserialization RCE
description: The preferences cookie uses node-serialize for deserialization, enabling RCE.
hint: Set a preferences cookie with a serialized object containing an IIFE: {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){return 'pwned'}()"}

name: Plaintext Credit Cards
description: Credit card numbers are stored and returned in plaintext in order responses.
hint: View any order's details or the order history - credit card numbers are fully visible.

name: DES Encryption with Hardcoded Key
description: The 'secure messaging' feature uses DES encryption with a hardcoded key.
hint: Check /api/v2/admin/debug for the DES key, or read config.js. The key is 'vulnc0rp'.

name: Predictable API Tokens
description: API tokens are generated using Math.random() instead of a cryptographically secure RNG.
hint: GET /api/v2/token/next generates tokens using Math.random() - they're predictable!

name: Predictable Password Reset Token
description: Password reset tokens are just timestamps converted to hex.
hint: GET /api/v2/reset-token/predict shows how tokens are generated: Date.now().toString(16)

name: Hardcoded JWT Secret
description: The JWT secret is 'secret'. Forge a JWT with admin privileges.
hint: Check /api/v2/admin/debug for the JWT secret, or config.js. Sign a JWT with {userId:1,role:'admin'}.

name: Credentials in Source Files
description: Real credentials are stored in .env.example and config.js source files.
hint: Read the .env.example file or the /api/v2/admin/debug endpoint for hardcoded secrets.

name: Sensitive Data in Logs
description: The application logs full request bodies including passwords and credit card numbers.
hint: Access /logs/app.log or GET /api/v2/logs to see all logged request data.

name: Log Injection
description: Unsanitized user input in log entries enables log injection/forging.
hint: Include newlines and fake timestamps in your request to forge log entries that frame another user.

name: Logs in Web Root
description: Application logs are stored in the web-accessible public/ directory.
hint: Navigate to /logs/app.log in your browser to download the complete log file.

name: Verbose Error Messages
description: Unhandled errors return full stack traces, file paths, and dependency versions.
hint: Trigger an error (e.g., invalid SQL) and observe the detailed stack trace in the response.

name: Server Technology Disclosure
description: HTTP response headers reveal the server technology stack.
hint: Check the Server and X-Powered-By headers in any HTTP response.

name: Auth Tokens in localStorage
description: Authentication tokens and user roles are stored in localStorage, accessible via XSS.
hint: After login, check localStorage for vulnlab_token, vulnlab_role, vulnlab_user keys.

name: Excessive PII in API Responses
description: User API endpoints return all PII (SSN, address, phone) even when not needed.
hint: GET /api/users/ or /api/users/1 returns SSN, password hash, security answers, and more.

name: Overly Permissive CORS
description: The API returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * allowing any origin to make requests.
hint: Check response headers. Create an HTML page on another origin that fetches data from the API.

name: SSRF via Webhook
description: The webhook testing feature allows SSRF to read local files and access internal services.
hint: POST /admin/webhooks/test with url=file:///etc/passwd to read server files.

name: Vulnerable Dependency
description: The application includes packages with known vulnerabilities.
hint: Run npm audit on the project to identify the vulnerable node-serialize package (CVE-2017-5941).

name: Remote Code via Plugin System
description: The plugin system fetches and eval()s JavaScript from user-supplied URLs.
hint: POST /admin/plugins/install with a URL pointing to a JS file. The server will eval() its contents.

name: Discover the Backdoor
description: A hidden backdoor route grants admin access with specific query parameters.
hint: Check robots.txt for /backdoor. Access /backdoor?debug=true&grant=admin while logged in.

name: No Subresource Integrity
description: External scripts and stylesheets are loaded without SRI hashes.
hint: Check index.html - the Google Fonts link has no integrity attribute.

name: Coupon Code Stacking
description: Multiple coupon codes can be applied to a single order for excessive discounts.
hint: Apply the same coupon multiple times, or use the couponCodes array in the checkout request body.

name: Self-Referral Credits
description: The referral system doesn't validate if the referrer and referred are the same person.
hint: POST /api/orders/referral with your own API token as the referralCode.

name: Order Replay Attack
description: Submitting the same order token multiple times processes the order multiple times.
hint: Use the same orderToken in multiple checkout requests. The server doesn't reject duplicates.

name: Race Condition - Buy Last Item Twice
description: Two simultaneous purchase requests can both succeed for the last item in stock.
hint: The 'Limited Edition Badge' has stock=1. Send two checkout requests simultaneously.

name: Web Shell Upload
description: File upload has no server-side file type validation. Upload and execute a web shell.
hint: Upload a .ejs file, then access it via /files/render/yourfile.ejs to execute server-side code.

name: Path Traversal Upload
description: Unsanitized filenames allow path traversal to write files outside the upload directory.
hint: Upload a file with filename like ../../server/routes/pwned.js to overwrite server files.

name: Template Execution via Upload
description: Uploaded .ejs templates are rendered by the server, enabling server-side code execution.
hint: Upload an .ejs file with <%= process.env %> and access it via /files/render/yourfile.ejs

name: Path Traversal Download
description: The download endpoint allows path traversal to read any file on the server.
hint: GET /files/download?filename=../../server/config.js or filename=../../etc/passwd

name: GET Request Deletes Product
description: All HTTP methods are accepted on all routes. A GET request can trigger product deletion.
hint: Visit /api/products/delete/1 in your browser (GET request) to delete product #1.

name: Mass Assignment - Register as Admin
description: User registration accepts a 'role' field in the request body, directly setting it in the database.
hint: POST /auth/register with {"role": "admin"} in the request body.

name: GraphQL Introspection Data Leak
description: GraphQL has introspection enabled and no authorization. Query all users, orders, and secrets.
hint: Visit /graphql and run: { users { username passwordHash ssn } } or { secretFlag }

name: Git Directory Exposed
description: The .git directory is accessible from the web root, exposing source code and config.
hint: Access /.git/config to see the repository configuration including the internal Git URL.

name: Source Maps Exposed
description: JavaScript source maps are served publicly, exposing original source code.
hint: Build the client and check for .map files in the client/dist/assets/ directory.

name: Vulnerable npm Packages
description: package.json includes packages with known CVEs (node-serialize has CVE-2017-5941).
hint: Run 'npm audit' in the project directory to identify vulnerable packages.

name: Hidden Endpoints via robots.txt
description: robots.txt lists all 'hidden' admin and sensitive paths.
hint: Access /robots.txt - it helpfully lists every secret path including admin debug endpoints.

name: Public Swagger Documentation
description: Internal API documentation is publicly accessible at /swagger.json.
hint: Access /swagger.json to see all documented endpoints including internal/admin ones.

name: No Security Headers
description: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, or other security headers are set.
hint: Check response headers - no CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or HSTS.

name: Clickjacking - No X-Frame-Options
description: The app is frameable (no clickjacking protection). Create a clickjacking attack page.
hint: Create an HTML page with an iframe loading VulnLab's change-password form, overlaid with a deceptive UI.

name: Bypass Rate Limit via X-Forwarded-For
description: Rate limiting uses the X-Forwarded-For header for IP identification, which is spoofable.
hint: Set difficulty to medium, then send requests with different X-Forwarded-For headers to bypass rate limiting.

name: Host Header Injection
description: The Host header is reflected into password reset URLs without validation.
hint: POST /auth/forgot-password-link with Host: evil.com header. The reset link will point to evil.com.

name: SSRF Internal Service Access
description: Use SSRF to access internal services via the webhook tester.
hint: Try url=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v2/admin/debug to access internal endpoints via SSRF.

name: No Password Complexity
description: There are no password complexity requirements. Users can register with password '1'.
hint: Register a new account with password '1' - it succeeds without any complexity check.

name: Session Cookie No HttpOnly
description: Session cookies have no HttpOnly flag, making them accessible via JavaScript/XSS.
hint: After login, run document.cookie in the browser console to see the session cookie.

name: Client-Side Only Access Control
description: The admin link is hidden in the UI for non-admins, but all admin API endpoints are accessible.
hint: Navigate directly to /admin in your browser as a regular user, or call /admin/dashboard API.

name: Price Override in Checkout
description: Product prices can be overridden in the checkout request body.
hint: In the checkout POST body, include an 'items' object with custom prices: {"items":{"1":{"price":0.01}}}

name: MD5 Password Hashing
description: Passwords are hashed with MD5 and no salt, making them trivially crackable.
hint: Export users via /api/v2/users/export and look up the MD5 hashes on crackstation.net.

name: Search History in Cookie
description: Recent searches are stored in a plaintext cookie.
hint: Search for something on the products page, then check the 'recentSearch' cookie.

name: No Cache-Control Headers
description: Sensitive data responses have no Cache-Control headers, allowing browser caching.
hint: Check response headers on /api/users/profile - no Cache-Control, Pragma, or Expires headers.

name: No HTTPS Enforcement
description: The application doesn't enforce HTTPS and has no HSTS header.
hint: All traffic is over HTTP. Check response headers - no Strict-Transport-Security header.

name: GraphQL DoS via Deep Nesting
description: GraphQL has no query depth limiting, enabling DoS via deeply nested queries.
hint: Send a deeply nested query: { users { orders { user { orders { user { orders { ... } } } } } } }

name: Debug Mode Enabled
description: Debug mode is enabled in the environment (DEBUG=*).
hint: Check the docker-compose.yml or /api/v2/admin/debug - DEBUG=* is set in environment.

name: Negative Quantity Free Items
description: Adding items with negative quantity results in a negative total, effectively getting paid to 'buy'.
hint: Add an expensive item to cart, change quantity to -5, then checkout. Total becomes negative.

name: No File Size Limit
description: No server-side file size limit is enforced on uploads.
hint: Upload a very large file - the server accepts it without any size restriction.

name: GraphQL Admin Mutation Without Auth
description: GraphQL mutations (updateUserRole, deleteProduct) require no authentication.
hint: Run: mutation { updateUserRole(userId: 2, role: "admin") { username role } } without any auth.

name: Brute Force Login
description: The login endpoint has no effective rate limiting. Brute force the admin password.
hint: Send many login attempts to /auth/login. In easy mode there is no rate limiting at all.

name: View Any Order by ID
description: View any order by iterating order IDs - no ownership check.
hint: GET /api/orders/1, /api/orders/2, etc. The server returns any order regardless of who placed it.

name: SQL Error Reveals Schema
description: SQL errors return the full query including the injected input, revealing database structure.
hint: Search for a single quote to trigger a SQL error that shows the full query structure.

name: Passwords Logged in Plaintext
description: Login requests log the full body including the plaintext password.
hint: Login, then check /logs/app.log - your password appears in the logged request body.

name: CSRF No Token Validation
description: No CSRF tokens are used. Forms can be submitted from any origin.
hint: Create an HTML form on another page that POSTs to /api/users/change-password. No CSRF protection.
